newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania sees '96 sugar output, imports at 250,000T.
newsitem.headline: Romania sees '96 sugar output, imports at 250,000T.

text.p: Romania's 1996 sugar output is expected to amount to some 250,000 tonnes, raising the prospect of imports of about the same quantity, an agriculture ministry official said on Monday.

The ministry expected a crop of around 2.7 million tonnes of sugar beet this year. "If harvesting is done in time and losses kept at a minimum we might get around 250,000 tonnes of white sugar," the official said.
"Romania will have to import some 250,000 tonnes of raw sugar to meet demand of both population and industry this year," the official said.
Data show the country imported 246,489 tonnes of sugar last year and 90,230 during January-May 1996.
Beet harvesting usually starts in Romania by October.
An acute shortage of funds and fuel which hit the farming sector recently might affect sugar beet harvesting, too, the ministry official said without elaborating.

A source in the sugar sector said beet on 23,000 hectares of the 161,950 sown had been lost due to a harsh winter and late snows. Lack of proper machinery, inadequate storage, transport delays and other probelsm might cause further losses, the source said.
The remaining beet "looked fine" and tests showed sugar content amounted to 12.4 percent.
Only 24 of 33 sugar factories are operational with a total capacity of 62,000 tonnes of beet a day, data show.
Beet output has been in continuous decline in recent years, reflecting poor management of crop lands and a lack of funds.
Farmers had used only 100 kilos of fertiliser per hectare, compared with a recommended 160 kilos.
Many farmers had given up growing sugar beet after factories failed to pay them in time for the 1995 crop, the source said.
